idiom-31-q11.truthCondition: Oliver and his brother are once again arguing fiercely over who should use the bathroom first.
idiom-31-q11.correctReason: 原題的「another」表示兩兄弟又再爭吵；正確句保留了浴室使用次序這個爭議。

foils.text: Oliver and his brother fight like cat and dog over who should clean the bathroom first.
foils.reason: 這句把爭議由「誰先用浴室」改成「誰先清潔浴室」。

foils.text: Oliver and his brother are fighting like cat and dog for the first time over the bathroom.
foils.reason: 「for the first time」表示第一次爭吵，與原題的「又再」不符。

foils.text: Oliver and his brother agree about who should use the bathroom first this time.
foils.reason: 這句說兩人已達成共識，抹去了原題正在發生的激烈爭吵。

idiom-31-q12.truthCondition: Two shop owners have argued fiercely for years over the space outside their shops.
idiom-31-q12.correctReason: 「have been fighting」配合「for years」，保留店主多年來持續爭奪店外空間的意思。

foils.text: The two shop owners fought like cat and dog once over the space outside their shops.
foils.reason: 「once」把多年反覆爭吵改成單次爭執。

foils.text: The two shop owners have been fighting like cat and dog for years over their shop signs.
foils.reason: 這句把爭議由店外空間改成店舖招牌。

foils.text: The two shop owners have been sharing the space outside their shops peacefully for years.
foils.reason: 這句說店主一直和平共用空間，與多年激烈爭吵相反。

idiom-31-q13.truthCondition: Sophie and her cousin argued fiercely throughout the family dinner.
idiom-31-q13.correctReason: 正確句保留蘇菲與表親這兩人，以及從晚餐開始到結束一直激烈爭吵的時間範圍。

foils.text: Sophie and her cousin fought like cat and dog before the family dinner began.
foils.reason: 「before ... began」把爭吵移到晚餐開始之前；原題說爭吵發生並持續於席間。

foils.text: Sophie and her cousin fought like cat and dog briefly during the family dinner.
foils.reason: 「briefly」表示只短暫爭吵；原題說兩人整頓飯都在爭執。

foils.text: Sophie and her cousin spoke calmly throughout the family dinner.
foils.reason: 「spoke calmly」把持續激烈的爭吵改成平靜交談。

idiom-31-q14.truthCondition: Liam and Noah will argue angrily all the time if they must share a room.
idiom-31-q14.correctReason: 正確句把爭吵繫於「必須共用一間房」的條件，並以慣用語表達激烈反覆的爭執。

foils.text: Liam and Noah will fight like cat and dog unless they have to share one room.
foils.reason: 「unless」把條件倒轉：這句說不共用房間才會吵。

foils.text: Liam and Noah will fight like cat and dog once if they share one room.
Liam and Noah will get along well if they have to share one room.
foils.reason: 這句預測兩人相處融洽，與原題預測的激烈爭吵相反。

idiom-31-q15.truthCondition: The project partners may begin arguing angrily if no one helps them agree on the plan.
idiom-31-q15.correctReason: 原題只是說若無人協助達成共識，拍檔「可能」開始激烈爭吵；正確句保留條件和不確定性。

foils.text: The two project partners will certainly start fighting like cat and dog if nobody helps them agree on the plan.
foils.reason: 「will certainly」把原題的「可能」改成必然，超出已知資訊。

foils.text: The two project partners may start fighting like cat and dog if nobody helps them choose a team name.
foils.reason: 這句把需要協商的「計劃」改成「隊名」。

foils.text: The two project partners may stop fighting like cat and dog if nobody helps them agree on the plan.
foils.reason: 「stop」表示停止爭吵，原題說他們可能因此開始爭吵。
